criteria.keep_wide: Affirm the status quo boundary: revocation protection comes from re-asserting one deployment-wide revision at commit plus live revalidation of permission and revocation, so every intervening write — related or not — voids the commit. Enrollment records stay explanatory. Rationale for keeping: smallest proven surface, no new proof obligations, uniform rule every author already follows. Rationale against: couples independent tenants through shared version movement, multiplies retries as write load grows, repeats predicate work on each mutation, and leaves D1 contention as the principal unmeasured hazard.
criteria.narrow: Move the boundary inward: revocation protection comes from re-checking exactly the enrolled membership and record dependencies at commit, so only movement in what the operation touched voids it. Rationale for moving: removes cross-tenant invalidation coupling, cuts spurious retries, keeps the fence proportional to the operation. Rationale against: demands fresh assertion bookkeeping with a D1 durability case, a second fence semantic to specify, test, and document, and confidence that every authorizing read is in fact enrolled ( gaps would silently authorize).

fence_scope.instructions: Settle the parked T32a remainder for B4: should the fence that guards fenced commits against mid-flight revocation remain the single database-wide revision check, or should it narrow to the enrolled per-team and per-record dependencies — judging strictly by safety preservation against coupling and proof burden?

request.state: Context: CanLang state engine, T32b checkpoint fence, the checkpoint_fence alternative adopted at T32a. Inspection-verified. (1) Commit path: the engine re-asserts the settled revision without exception and revalidates permission and revocation live; a commit survives only if nothing was written after its checkpoint. (2) Dependency enrollment: state-dependent reads join the owner checkpoint tagged by kind (membership: team plus user; record: version seen); the tags are presently used to attribute invalidations and to keep the narrower-fence question alive. (3) Eventual reads are display-only and rejected as authorizers everywhere. (4) Documented downsides of the wide check: authority-layer failure coupling (distant membership writes cancel local operations), contention-driven conflict growth, twice-paid predicate cost, and D1 contention as the foremost unmeasured runtime exposure. (5) Documented loose ends: compound gates admittable absent caller membership risk false voiding (suite never routes compounds through invoke; permanent fix is a mechanism-owned by-aware check), and revocation versus an already-fenced batch needs a storage-atomicity answer for durable proof. (6) T32a adopted the fence and explicitly deferred the wide-vs-narrow scope call. Zero contention measurements; zero production traffic.
